correctness.rationale: For every h>=1,k>=1, the Fibonacci companion matrix Q satisfies Q^p=-Q^{-1} and Q^(p^2)=Q modulo odd inert primes p=2,3 mod 5; the odd-binomial coefficients of (p+h)^(2k) are even. Therefore F_((p+h)^(2k))=F_((h-1)^(2k)) mod p, while a_1=F_((h+1)^(2k)); their difference is a fixed nonzero integer Delta. Infinitely many inert primes by Dirichlet avoid M*Delta for any fixed M, contradicting the prime-index Dold condition. For h=0, the positive 5-multiplier is supplied by the explicitly credited Moss-Ward Cor.3, and n=5 Dold forces 5|M. The h=1 and index-1 boundaries are handled; 24 inert primes times 40 h,k cases were independently checked, but the infinity assertion rests on proof, not enumeration.
